vulnerability_sections.findings_text: Analysis of MirrCast suggests a high level of risk associated with code vulnerabilities. Ten activities (including MainActivity, BrowserActivity, and WebActivity) are exported without protection, making them accessible to any other app on the device. The app allows its data to be backed up via adb, and it can be installed on Android 6.0-6.0.1, a range with multiple unpatched platform vulnerabilities that Google no longer supports with reasonable security updates. The app uses the MD5 and SHA-1 hashing algorithms, both vulnerable to collision attacks, and multiple hardcoded API keys and credentials were recovered from the app bundle. The app also declares custom URL schemes and a deep-link host, which need review for hijacking or spoofing risk.

checks.check: Unprotected Exported Activity
checks.explanation: 10 activities are exported without protection, including MainActivity, VideoPlayActivity, BrowserActivity, WebActivity, TranslucentActivity, PlayFeedbackActivity, ImaAdActivity, AdPlayActivity, AdDefaultActivity, and GdprBreakActivity. Any other app on the device can launch these activities.

checks.check: Application Data can be Backed Up
checks.explanation: The manifest sets android:allowBackup=true. This allows anyone with USB debugging access to copy application data off the device via adb.

checks.check: App can be Installed on a Vulnerable/Unpatched Minimum SDK Version
checks.explanation: minSdk=23 allows installation on Android 6.0-6.0.1, which has multiple unfixed vulnerabilities and no longer receives reasonable security updates from Google.

checks.check: Application Uses Custom URL Schemes / Deep Links
checks.explanation: BrowserActivity registers http:// and https:// schemes, and WebActivity registers a custom tv:// scheme with host com.tv.casttv. These handlers need review for hijacking or unsafe parameter handling.

checks.check: Uses SHA-1 Hashing Algorithm
checks.explanation: SHA-1 is a weak hash known to have hash collisions.
checks.compliance: CWE-327; OWASP Top 10: M5-Insufficient Cryptography; MASVS-CRYPTO-4

checks.check: Uses MD5 Hashing Algorithm
checks.explanation: MD5 is a weak hash known to have hash collisions.
checks.compliance: CWE-327; OWASP Top 10: M5-Insufficient Cryptography; MASVS-CRYPTO-4

checks.check: Contains Hard-coded Cryptographic Key / Credentials
checks.explanation: Multiple hardcoded values were recovered from the app bundle, including a Google API key, a Firebase Crashlytics mapping ID, and default settings/AirPlay credentials.

checks.check: Insecure Encryption Mode (CBC with PKCS5/PKCS7 Padding)
checks.explanation: The app uses the CBC encryption mode with PKCS5/PKCS7 padding, which is vulnerable to padding oracle attacks.
checks.compliance: CWE-649; OWASP Top 10: M5-Insufficient Cryptography; MASVS-CRYPTO-3

checks.check: Components with Known Vulnerabilities
checks.explanation: No known-vulnerable dependency versions were flagged in this scan.

checks.check: Application Utilizes Insecure Random Number Generator
checks.explanation: No use of a weak/predictable random number source (e.g. java.util.Random for security decisions) was identified in this scan.

checks.check: Weak PBKDF2 or Key-Derivation Parameters
checks.explanation: No PBKDF2 or other key-derivation calls with insufficient iteration counts were identified in this scan.

checks.check: Cryptographic Key Generation Not Using Approved Platform APIs (Android Keystore)
checks.explanation: No ad hoc key-generation calls bypassing Android Keystore were identified in this scan.

vulnerability_sections.findings_text: Analysis of MirrCast suggests a high level of risk associated with networking. The app's network security configuration permits cleartext traffic to all domains and trusts user-installed certificate authorities, meaning a device with a malicious CA installed could intercept and modify the app's TLS traffic without detection. Cleartext traffic is also enabled at the manifest level. No API authentication weaknesses were identified in the strings or traffic captured during this scan.

checks.check: Network Security Configuration Allows Cleartext Traffic
checks.explanation: The base network security configuration is insecurely configured to permit cleartext traffic to all domains.

checks.check: Network Security Configuration Allows User-installed CAs
checks.explanation: The base configuration is set to trust user-installed certificates, which enables man-in-the-middle attacks if a malicious CA is present on the device.

checks.check: Clear Text Traffic is Enabled for App
checks.explanation: android:usesCleartextTraffic=true is set at the application level.

checks.check: Application Vulnerable to Janus Vulnerability
checks.explanation: The app is signed with the v1 signature scheme (in addition to v2/v3), which makes it vulnerable to the Janus vulnerability on Android 5.0-8.0 devices.

checks.check: API Authentication Weakness (weak token handling / API key used as authentication)
checks.explanation: No weak API-authentication patterns (e.g. API keys used as sole user authentication) were identified in this scan.

vulnerability_sections.findings_text: Anti-VM and anti-debug checks (Build.FINGERPRINT, Build.MODEL, Build.MANUFACTURER, and related device-property checks, plus a Debug.isDebuggerConnected() check) were identified across the app's classes.dex files, indicating some environment-tampering awareness. No explicit root-detection or biometric-bypass-resistance logic was identified in this scan.

checks.check: Anti-VM / Anti-Emulator Checks Present
checks.explanation: classes.dex, classes2.dex, and classes3.dex each contain Build.FINGERPRINT/MODEL/MANUFACTURER/PRODUCT/HARDWARE/BOARD/TAGS and SIM/network-operator checks consistent with anti-VM logic.

checks.check: Anti-Debug Code Present
checks.explanation: classes3.dex contains a Debug.isDebuggerConnected() check.

checks.check: Components Contain Debug Symbols
checks.explanation: No stripped-symbol gaps were flagged for the app's native libraries in this scan.

checks.check: Root Detection Missing
checks.explanation: Root-detection presence or absence was not independently confirmed in this scan; recommend dynamic verification.

checks.check: Biometric / Local Authentication Bypass Possible
checks.explanation: The app was not observed to implement local biometric authentication gates in this scan.

vulnerability_sections.findings_text: Analysis of MirrCast suggests a medium level of risk associated with data storage. The app can read from and write to external storage, which is world-readable and may be analyzed or modified by other applications. Source files disclose a hardcoded IP address, and the app logs information to the device log, which should never include sensitive values in production builds. No sensitive values were identified specifically in SharedPreferences or HTTP cache databases during this scan.

checks.check: App can Read/Write to External Storage
checks.explanation: Any app on the device can read data written to external storage by this app.
checks.compliance: CWE-276; OWASP Top 10: M2-Insecure Data Storage; MSTG-STORAGE-2

checks.check: IP Address Disclosure
checks.explanation: Hardcoded IP address references were found in the app's code.

checks.check: The App Logs Information to Device Logs
checks.explanation: Sensitive information should never be logged in production builds.

checks.check: Sensitive Values Stored Insecurely in SharedPreferences
checks.explanation: No sensitive values (credentials, tokens, PII) were identified in SharedPreferences during this scan.

checks.check: Sensitive Data in HTTP Cache Databases
checks.explanation: No sensitive values were identified in WebView/HTTP cache databases during this scan.

checks.check: Sensitive Data Exposed Through Deep Link / URL Handler
checks.explanation: The registered tv:// and http(s):// handlers were not observed passing sensitive data in this scan.
